annotationRationale: The central tasks are handling exact floor intervals and summing the resulting arithmetic progression. A direct monotonicity calculation proves uniqueness of the fractional-part ratio. The supplied quadratic and reciprocal parameterizations describe the same progression, so they are consolidated into one method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, a=29/900 gives exactly x=0 and x=30n/29 for 1≤n≤28. Their sum is 420, and p+q=929 matches choice C. No statement, choice, or grading contradiction appears.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. Random Math's first solution contributes the retained fractional-part ratio, and its second contributes the retained interval-sum bounds. LIVE's reciprocal parameter and Random Math's third quadratic computation describe the same solution family, so separate routes would add little.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed floor/fractional-part and arithmetic-sequence-sum concepts are central. Definition-based monotonicity is appropriately supporting. The unused quadratic concepts were correctly removed from this route.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The sign and integer exclusions are correct. The displayed difference proves strict increase of t/(1+t)^2 on (0,1), so all positive solutions share one ratio. Exactly the indices nt<1 are valid. Summing n<x_n<n+1 forces N=28; then 406(1+t)=420 gives t=1/29. The strict endpoint excludes n=29, and 29/900 is reduced.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited references support the claimed ingredients. The explanation reconstructs their mathematics with an explicit uniqueness proof and rigorous bounds, rather than reproducing the sources' heuristic transitions. The source-informed-original designation correctly identifies nonofficial third-party influence.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains the ratio substitution, the monotonicity calculation is fully shown, and the converse floor restriction establishes completeness. The difficult count and endpoint are reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three immediate nodes match the written work: exact floor intervals, monotonicity by subtraction, and arithmetic-sequence summation. No additional node is needed for the derived solution family.
